item.content:encoded:
As flames engulfed a building in the heart of Mt Hagen City yesterday, panic and confusion gripped the area, with crowds gathering and opportunists attempting to take advantage of the unfolding disaster.

The fire broke out at the Green Leaf Chinese shop in Mt Hagen City around midday on Sunday (25-10-26), as the El Nino heat continued to affect the province and many residents attended church services.

But while the fire continued to consume the building, one senior police officer stepped forward to take charge, demonstrating the leadership and courage he has become known for during tribal conflicts, law-and-order disturbances and other emergencies in Western Highlands Province.

Western Highlands Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent John Sagom, who has also been appointed Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) for the Western End Divisional Command, led police personnel in securing the scene and preventing further disorder.

As smoke and flames rose from the building, crowds gathered from nearby settlements and surrounding areas, with some attempting to loot goods from the burning premises and neighboring shops along the arcade.

Police officers initially stood by as the situation unfolded before receiving orders to disperse the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Sagom then led local police personnel, supported by three units from Hela Province currently in Mt Hagen for training, to secure the area.

Their presence prevented opportunists from accessing the fire-damaged building, although five people were arrested for allegedly attempting to loot the premises.

The fire brigade arrived later, while local businessman Pat Duckworth provided three water trucks to assist in extinguishing the flames.

Some local youths also joined the emergency response, climbing onto the building's roof to help fight the fire.

Two Chinese nationals were rescued from the building before it collapsed internally.

Speaking at the scene, Chief Superintendent Sagom said the fire could have caused further damage had it spread to the National Development Bank (NDB), which shares the building with the Green Leaf shop.

He said a substantial amount of money and goods had been lost in the blaze.

Sagom also raised concerns over the increasing number of fires involving buildings in Mt Hagen City, noting that many of the affected structures were old and required the attention of the relevant authorities.

He called on city residents, particularly those living in settlements surrounding Mt Hagen, to respect police operations and stay away from emergency scenes.

He warned that attempting to loot or interfere with emergency responders would only bring trouble rather than benefit those involved.

The National Development Bank will remain closed for the time being while PNG Power conducts inspections to determine whether electrical issues contributed to the incident and that it might affect NDB.

As investigations continue, the incident has raised concerns over building safety, emergency preparedness and public behaviour during disasters in Mt Hagen City.

And as for Chief Superintendent Sagom and the officers who secured the scene, the immediate priority was to protect lives, prevent looting and maintain order while the emergency response continued.

item.title: Morobe 63rd annual show draws strong crowd
item.description: Morobe Show president Hans Mehl says the 63rd annual show has drawn strong crowds, reaching about three-quarters capacity by mid-morning despite a delayed start. Mehl said the morning programme was delayed after some security personnel arrived late, but the issues were resolved and activities were underway.
item.content:encoded:
Morobe Show president Hans Mehl says the 63rd annual show has drawn strong crowds, reaching about three-quarters capacity by mid-morning despite a delayed start.

Mehl said the morning programme was delayed after some security personnel arrived late, but the issues were resolved and activities were underway.

He said the fireworks display at Mount Lunaman on Friday night went well, while stallholders were active and visitors were enjoying the show.

Light rain briefly delayed ring events, but Mehl remained hopeful the weather would clear.

Motorbike displays, the Naked Koala band and parachutists carrying flags were among the attractions visitors were looking forward to.

Mehl said the strong early turnout was encouraging, with crowd numbers already at levels normally seen around midday.

item.title: Nari urges farmers to prepare for drought
item.description: Agronomist Rodney Aku of the National Agricultural Research Institute (NARI) Momase Regional Centre is urging farmers to establish reliable water sources and irrigation systems to protect their crops during dry conditions. Aku said access to water was particularly important during the first two weeks after planting, when crops were establishing their roots and needed sufficient moisture to grow.
item.content:encoded:
Agronomist Rodney Aku of the National Agricultural Research Institute (NARI) Momase Regional Centre is urging farmers to establish reliable water sources and irrigation systems to protect their crops during dry conditions.

Aku said access to water was particularly important during the first two weeks after planting, when crops were establishing their roots and needed sufficient moisture to grow.

He said NARI had received requests from non-government organisations and other agricultural partners for advice on planting drought-tolerant crops to help farmers prepare for dry conditions.

Aku warned that farmers without proper irrigation systems could struggle to maintain crop production as the soil dries out.

He said crops such as cucumbers, pumpkins and corn could be planted again if farmers had reliable irrigation systems to supply enough water.

Aku encouraged farmers to plan ahead by securing water sources and improving their irrigation systems to sustain food production during periods of drought.

item.title: Prolonged dry season escalates to ‘national humanitarian concern’
item.description: Many parts in Papua New Guinea are feeling the full force of the El Nino weather pattern, with devastating impacts now reported from the Highlands to the coastal provinces. What began as a prolonged dry spell has now escalated into a national humanitarian concern, affecting water, food, health and livelihoods.
item.content:encoded:
Many parts in Papua New Guinea are feeling the full force of the El Nino weather pattern, with devastating impacts now reported from the Highlands to the coastal provinces.

What began as a prolonged dry spell has now escalated into a national humanitarian concern, affecting water, food, health and livelihoods.

Across Simbu, months of little to no rain have dried up natural water sources. Rivers and creeks that communities depend on for drinking and washing are at their lowest levels in years.

Food gardens are failing. Kaukau, corn, greens and other staple crops are wilting and dying due to lack of moisture and excessive heat. Families are now facing food shortages, with many surviving on one meal a day.

Adding to the crisis are uncontrollable bushfires. The dry bush, kunai grass and forest floors have become highly flammable. Small garden fires or cooking fires are quickly spreading out of control, destroying homes, fences, coffee gardens and livestock.

Bob Tapie , OIC of Monono Sub Health center in Chuave said there is an increase case in flu, cough, diarrhoea and skin diseases as people are forced to drink from dirty water sources.

George Waikai, technical officer of the Simbu Provincial Disaster coordinator warned that if the dry spell continues, the situation will worsen into a major food and water crisis similar to the 2015 El Nino.

Behind these national statistics is the human face of the crisis. In the rural Kureiri village of Elimbari LLG in Chuave District if Simbu a father, James Koma, his wife and their five small children have been left homeless.

Their home was completely destroyed today by a bushfire fueled by the dry conditions.

Only charred posts remain, with smoke still rising from the ashes.

"We lost everything. Our house, our clothes, our bedding and our stored food - all burnt to ashes. We have nowhere to sleep," Koma said.

John Kuman Ward 5 Councilor, Elimbari LLG, Chuave said it is saddened to see the family suffer like this.

He said James is a hardworking father now lost everything.

Councilor Kuman is calling on the Chuave DDA and Simbu Provincial Government to urgently intervene to similar situations in the district.

" Not only James and family but last week similar incidents happened at Gorokabu with seven houses burnt to ashes. The Government must help. Our people need tarpaulins, food, clean water and medicines now", he said.

Provincial Disaster Offices across the Highlands have been urged to conduct rapid assessments and provide immediate relief as the country braces for more dry months ahead.

item.title: Star-studded Samoa down Kumuls
item.description: A dominant second half performance by Toa Samoa was just enough to get them a win over the PNG Kumuls this afternoon at the Santos National Football Stadium. The Kumuls delivered a brave effort in the first half to trail 14-6, but the Samoans came out strong in the second with more field possession which eventually led to a big 64-6 win.
item.content:encoded:
A dominant second half performance by Toa Samoa was just enough to get them a win over the PNG Kumuls this afternoon at the Santos National Football Stadium.

The Kumuls delivered a brave effort in the first half to trail 14-6, but the Samoans came out strong in the second with more field possession which eventually led to a big 64-6 win.

Despite the big win, Samoa Coach Ben Gardiner commended the Kumuls for giving them a good challenge in the first half.

“I thought the Kumuls were tremendous in the first half, it was an end-to-end game, very physical and I really want to congratulate Papua New Guinea on their performance, particularly in the first half,” Gardiner said.

Apart from the on field performance, Samoa captain Junior Paulo said they are so humbled by the reception and hospitality shown by passionate PNG fans.

“For us, we’ve been able to go out there and share rugby league with a nation that calls rugby league its national sport and we are humbled to share the experience with everyone,” Paulo said.

Meanwhile despite the loss, PNG Kumuls Coach Jason Demetriou commended the efforts delivered by his boys against a star-studded Samoan outfit.

The Samoans remain unbeaten will face Tonga in their next match while the Kumuls will travel to Sydney to face England.

Earlier, the PNG Orchids also went down to the Fiji Bulikulas 40-4.

item.title: Construction work for Kema and Melant primary schools in SHP continues
item.description: Students at Kema Primary School in Lai Valley LLG and the newly established Melant Primary School in Highway Karinz in the Mendi Munihu District of Southern Highlands Province will soon benefit from modern learning facilities, with construction of a 4-in-1 classroom complex at each school nearing completion. item.content:encoded:
Students at Kema Primary School in Lai Valley LLG and the newly established Melant Primary School in Highway Karinz in the Mendi Munihu District of Southern Highlands Province will soon benefit from modern learning facilities, with construction of a 4-in-1 classroom complex at each school nearing completion.

Despite challenges posed by the ongoing El Niño drought, communities have remained committed, ensuring work continues on schedule. Both projects are expected to be completed by the end of this month.

Mendi-Munihu MP Raphael Tonpi, said the new classrooms will ease overcrowding and create a more conducive environment for learning.

“When students learn in a clean, safe and well-maintained building, it sends a strong message that their education truly matters,” MP Tonpi said.

“This builds self-esteem, pride and school spirit. Upgraded facilities directly reduce absenteeism. Students are more motivated to attend school daily when the physical space is welcoming and comfortable,” he said.

He noted that cluttered, dark and overcrowded classrooms often increase stress and behavioural problems among students.

MP Tonpi said the projects are part of the Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority’s (MMDDA) broader plan to revive and restore vital government services in the district.

“Our people’s basic needs are accessible quality education and health services, roads and bridges, power and water, and improved church activities to support the spirituality of our people,” he said.

He described Melant Primary School as a historic milestone for the Highway Karinz community, which has not had a government-registered institution since Independence in 1975.

“Melant Primary School is the first of its kind for the community and is a gift from the MMDDA. Kema Primary is located in a very densely populated area, and this new complex will greatly improve teaching and learning,” MP Tonpi said.

The MP assured that service delivery will continue despite the upcoming elections.

“Even though elections are around the corner, the MMDDA will continue to deliver basic services for our people,” he said.

item.title: ​Kopiago LLG to host ‘gun surrender program’ next Friday
item.description: The Kopiago Local Level Government (LLG) in the Koroba Kopiago District of Hela Province is gearing up to host its official Gun Surrender Program next Friday, October 30, at Kopiago Station. ​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed the date following a recent visit to the LLG prior to attending the current Parliament Session.
item.content:encoded:
The Kopiago Local Level Government (LLG) in the Koroba Kopiago District of Hela Province is gearing up to host its official Gun Surrender Program next Friday, October 30, at Kopiago Station.

​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed the date following a recent visit to the LLG prior to attending the current Parliament Session.

​He confirmed that the disarmament program will resume following Parliament and will remain active until the state amnesty period officially expires on December 25.

​He urged all community members to actively participate in removing illegal firearms and commended local leaders and former warring factions for supporting the peace initiative, ​"I am confirming the date and calling on everyone to participate in this important program," Governor Undialu stated. "I want to thank all our community leaders and warring factions in Kopiago who have acknowledged this program. I urge you all to support it and make it a success."

​He emphasized that disarming communities is vital for restoring safety and unlocking future leadership representation for the LLG.

Talks are currently underway with the Electoral Commission of Papua New Guinea to stage by-elections for failed polls in Kopiago, the newly established Hewa LLG, and others.

​"The people need a leader to represent them," the Governor added. "While we wait for the Electoral Commission, I am calling on the people of Kopiago and Hewa LLGs to ensure guns are removed.

The gun culture has destroyed many communities, and everyone must unite to remove illegal guns and restore peace."

He said people holding unlicensed firearms in the district have two final chances to hand over their weapons under the amnesty grace period: Friday, October 30 at Kopiago Station and Saturday, October 31at Koroba Station.

​Governor Undialu warned that law enforcement will strictly enforce gun control laws once the amnesty period concludes.

​"People must respect and support this gun surrender initiative. No one will escape. There are people who will report, and police will catch you after the grace period ends," he warned.

​Following the Koroba-Kopiago, the surrender program team will advance to Komo-Hulia District before proceeding to Magarima District.

item.title: Western province submits SOE proposal
item.description: The Western Provincial government is calling on the national government to immediately declare State of Emergency in the province. This urgent cry for help follows severe impacts of El Nino affecting a population of over 300-hundred thousand and more than 65-thousand households.
item.content:encoded:
The Western Provincial government is calling on the national government to immediately declare State of Emergency in the province.

This urgent cry for help follows severe impacts of El Nino affecting a population of over 300-hundred thousand and more than 65-thousand households.

Water sources and crops have dried, leaving the people dying of starvation and battling with skin diseases as a result of the prolonged dry spell.

Being a landlocked province, their only access through the Fly River is cut off when the water level dropped, making is impossible for ships to deliver goods and services as well as medical supplies and threatening the lifeline of the Ok Tedi Mine.

With full endorsement from the four district MPs, the SoE proposal was formally handed over to the Minister for Health, National Emergency and Disaster Dr Billy Joseph, last night in Port Moresby.

The proposal also called for the National government to negotiate with the Indonesian government to open up the border post so people can have access to goods and services from Jayapura and also make it accessible for the OK Tedi mine to continue its operations.

When delivering the proposal, Governor Taboi Awi Yoto noted that a K25-million support funding set aside by the provincial government has been paid to suppliers of essential food supplies and water, however delivering the supplies to the people remains a challenge.

The province is calling on the government, development and bilateral partners for immediate assistance in getting the critically needed supplies to the people.

Minister Joseph received the proposal and assured the leaders that a SoE declaration is possible given the circumstances surrounding the province, however the National Executive Council will deliberate on it and respond at the soonest possible.

Meantime, the respective district MPs are delivering much needed relief supplies to the people with whatever little funding they have available.

item.title: Drought leaves Kapao families eating once a day
item.description: Families in Kapao in Menyama District are eating just one meal a day, drinking dirty creek water and struggling to send their children to school as a prolonged drought destroys food gardens and dries up water sources across 11 wards.

item.title: Fire destroys homes and church in SHP
item.description: A tragic fire fueled by strong winds has left a family in Southern Highlands province homeless and destitute after destroying several homes, a church, and properties estimated to worth over K200,000.
